# R365 — Production comparison and capture route for prefill scratch alias

Date: 2026-10-13 (JST). Read-only route audit. Candidate W is `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/feat-prefill-scratch-lifetime-alias-20261013`, base `410904c`; comparator checkout C is `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/feat-fixed-history-logits-comparator-20261013`. Main's sourceLLVM build session 60676 remained untouched. No execution, import, build, test, AST, lint, GPU/profiler, process/service/reset, Git, cleanup, or source changes were performed. This report makes no runtime, parity, quality, or production qualification claim.

## Finding

The smallest existing production inference path for full-history logits is the standalone native-pack route using `--spec-follow` and `--dump-logits`, with `STRATA_VERIFY_SEGMENTED=1` set before launch. It exercises batched prefill followed by the normal verifier and contiguous-prefix commit path. Each emitted row is full-vocabulary FP32; row `i` predicts `follow[i]` at absolute position `P-1+i`. Keep N follow IDs exactly, `--max-new N`, `--logits-stride 1`, `--stop-eos` off, no `--serve`, no `--prefill-until`, no early termination, and verify exact header/bytes and all positions/targets. It can produce valid paired distribution evidence once capture provenance and runtime lifecycle are attested; it does not establish alias state parity by itself.

The C `tools/fixed_history_logits.py` reader is strict about row count, byte length, finite every-vocabulary values, history identity, positions and lifecycle receipt fields. It computes per-row target logprob/NLL and both full-vocabulary KL directions, target rank, top-1/top-2 margin, top-1 agreement and quantiles. It does not compare raw prose, require generated text equality, set a universal tolerance, or make an adoption decision. The module hardcodes `production_capture_qualified: false` and `quality_qualified: false`; its receipt schema remains a NEW adapter contract. No reviewed production adapter currently certifies observed/reaped process lifecycle, output close/row count, fresh fault evidence and that the actual binary/source/runtime used the segmented native provider. Therefore numerical JSON from this reader cannot currently be represented as a qualified production result even if a future capture exists.

## Persistent state and SAVE/RESTORE reality

Standalone capture has no CLI for a state checkpoint or SAVE/RESTORE around `--spec-follow`. `--dump-residual` is only final residual for head bisection; `--dump-layers` records layer residuals on the session path, not GDN/QSA/PLE persistent state. The `--serve SAVE/RESTORE` path exists for conversations, but it is coupled to serving/session request semantics and is not a clean capture mode for standalone fixed follow. Reusing its files as an alias comparator would add route and session differences and still would not yield row-by-row logits in a fixed-history request.

The lowest-level usable state mechanism already exists: `conversation_checkpoint_save/restore` in `src/core/conversation_state.cpp` captures/restores GDN recurrent state plus convolution history, PLE normalized history, and indexer tails/dead keys/block position. `conversation_snapshot_save/restore` additionally copies each QSA KV layer and the draft KV using format-aware `conversation_kv_save`, which includes the actual K/V representation and indexer pooled rows. The public conversation machinery requires a token/image view and draft state, and snapshot validation binds geometry, layer ownership, context positions and cache metadata. That is more reliable than raw ad-hoc pointer copies, but there is no existing standalone callsite that writes such a snapshot at the desired comparison boundary.

Minimum persistent-state hook: add a default-off standalone diagnostic checkpoint at a clearly named committed token boundary (at least after the whole fixed-history run; preferably also after the final prompt token has been processed and after each accepted commit). Use the existing conversation snapshot API with exact committed token IDs and the live session/draft states; write one snapshot per arm plus an explicit position/geometry/encoding manifest and SHA-256. Alias OFF and ON must use identical model, history and offset. Compare decoded state numerically and structurally: FP32 GDN recurrence/conv and PLE history, exact QSA KV codes/scales/indexer cells where encoding is integral, and declared tolerances for floating state. Restore each snapshot into a fresh equivalent session and process the same next continuation; compare next logits and resulting state. This validates persistent continuation behavior and the real restore consumer. The current comparator accepts only raw logits captures and has no state artifact parser or state comparison fields, so a small companion state comparator/manifest (or explicit adapter extension) is needed; do not force state into the logits binary.

## Boundary coverage for alias-induced batching

`m.region_bytes` is consumed by batched PLE and `draft_kv`; alias ON can lower it and therefore change PLE `SB` or trigger the draft batch fallback even though arithmetic kernels are unchanged. A whole-prompt logits comparison sees downstream numerical effects but does not identify which subbatch caused them. Snapshotting only after the full prompt can also hide a transient difference later overwritten by history shifts.

Minimum diagnostics should record actual chunk positions/T and actual PLE SB for every PLE subbatch in both arms. At each outer prompt chunk tail, capture the full persistent session state. For each internal PLE subbatch tail, capture PLE history (and, if an actual state difference arises, add a full checkpoint around that boundary). In the verifier continuation, `--dump-logits` already covers every row; state checkpoints should be taken after commit, never from uncommitted speculative rows. Ensure the forced sequence reaches a full verifier window and a short tail window, and arrange the prefill token count so production chunking includes the normal final short chunk. Run any `draft_kv` boundary case separately if alias mode crosses its `B<64` fallback. This is bounded diagnostic capture, not a stock timing run.

The `--dump-logits` format is 8-byte `{int32 vocab,int32 rows}` followed by `rows*vocab` row-major FP32 values, with no embedded prompt/follow IDs, positions, model identity, route or capture status. Comparator metadata must bind those out of band. Its current manifest limits N and capture bytes, validates full exact positions `P-1..P+N-2`, requires all follow targets, and rejects NaN/Inf anywhere. Require a declared byte budget before allocating/capturing: each arm is `8 + 4*vocab*N`; both raw files plus state snapshots and receipts need a separate combined budget. Keep complete captures only through validated metrics/state comparison, then retire under ARTIFACT_RETENTION's serialized deletion manifest. Never use these captures for timing or change the stock `bench.sh --long --runs 3` path.

## Minimal ranked work before qualification

1. Preserve fixed-history production producer: existing standalone native pack, explicit segmented override, identical no-MTP recipe/config in both arms, exact prompt/follow IDs and effective source/compiler/runtime/profile/build. Disable MTP and suffix/lookup drafts consistently when isolating the main model; retain same `--spec` so verifier route is controlled. Do not use `--serve` for this producer.
2. Add only default-off state/boundary instrumentation needed for this question: committed-token snapshot boundary via conversation snapshot APIs; chunk/T and PLE-SB records; exact row positions and targets in a sidecar. Any new file schema needs version, hashes, endian/format, consumer, byte budget and retirement point. State outputs must contain all GDN/conv, QSA K/V plus indexer and PLE state needed to restore; a final residual or logits dump is insufficient.
3. Implement/review the production capture adapter for the existing comparator receipt from real supervisor/PID/reap, close and exact-row evidence, source/build/provider/runtime pins, segmented setting and fresh bounded fault checks. It must derive evidence, not synthesize success booleans from a command recipe. If no qualified adapter is ready, numerical metrics remain useful internal evidence but `production_capture_qualified=false`.
4. Extend comparison output with per-state-block exact equality or max/mean/RMS absolute and relative errors, per-position logits metrics, restore-continuation results and per-chunk/per-PLE-subbatch identity. Choose practical numerical/state interpretation from A/A repeat variation and intended behavior; exact full-state or prose identity is not a universal gate. Reject wrong positions, missing blocks, nonfinite data, incomplete/faulted runs and failed restore regardless of metric averages.
5. Keep capture, persistent-state numerical evidence, held-out task quality, operational fault evidence and quiet performance as separate outcomes. A successful numerical screen does not establish broad model quality. Run unchanged official quiet `bench.sh --long --runs 3` only in the existing serialized window and only after candidate runtime gates; preserve its performance rows and do not mix custom capture overhead into them.

## Unsupported combinations and limits

- `--serve` has no fixed-history full-logit producer, while `--spec-follow` is standalone-only. Scoring served mode-1 requests would require a new default-off fixed-follow hook in that serial serve verifier loop (capture emitted full rows before buffer reuse, keep normal commit logic, report positions/targets); pipeline/batching must stay off until separately covered. Conversation SAVE/RESTORE is not a replacement.
- `--prefill-until`, EOS/early stop, shortened follow, invalid IDs, stride above 1, canceled/forced/deadline/budget-hit captures, and unsegmented verifier route cannot satisfy exact-N evidence. Current CLI can silently truncate follow to `min(N, follow.size())`, so prevalidation and exact output/header/file-size checks are mandatory.
- Current comparison tool has no GDN/conv/QSA/PLE state ingestion, no chunk/subbatch evidence, no restore-continuation validation, and no qualified producer adapter. Existing source snapshot API materially reduces implementation scope but does not make these gaps disappear.
- R363 already handled alias readers/ownership; R356/R357 handled byte arithmetic. This pass adds no re-proof or new byte arithmetic. Changed batching remains a runtime gate.
- Existing B570 32049-token runs are below the 32768 minimum for the original quiet performance eligibility and do not constitute model quality coverage. Current upstream quiet COPY pair status is separately recorded in the supplied v185 registry (894 entries); this report neither reads private environment JSON nor modifies that registry. The quiet route remains unchanged.

- Candidate `src/core/verify.cpp`: segmented override and wait/read boundaries (`415–421`, `1514–1620`); verifier committed state lifecycle (`2384+`).

- Prior records: R319 production fixed-history route; R323 segmented standalone versus serve handoff; R331 binary/row/comparator contract; R336 quality interpretation; alias implementation note; R363 reader boundaries; comparator source-only contract v1. Current comparator capture adapter is expressly unqualified.

No source was changed, no capture was made, and no execution or quality conclusion is claimed.
